text: The proximity-labeling technique that fuses a promiscuous biotin ligase to a bait protein, biotinylating nearby proteins within about a 10 nm radius for later streptavidin capture, is called ___ (or its faster variant, TurboID).
explanation: BioID fuses a promiscuous biotin ligase to a bait protein so that proteins within roughly a 10 nm radius become biotinylated in living cells, after which streptavidin pulldown and mass spectrometry identify the labeled interactors. Its key advantage over AP-MS is the ability to capture transient and membrane-associated interactions that classical pulldowns often miss.
